skill.name: web-artifacts-builder
skill.description: Builds multi-file React artifacts with TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui, then bundles them into one HTML file.
skill.summary: Creates React-based Claude artifacts and packages them as single HTML files.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown code fences, safe command substitutions, local config edits, and documentation URLs. The meaningful risks are community shell scripts that install npm packages, modify project files, and delete local build outputs during bundling. No evidence found of prompt injection or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, avoid global installs when possible, and document that npm lifecycle scripts may run.

remediation.issue: Destructive cleanup in the bundle script
remediation.suggestion: Limit cleanup to generated build paths or prompt before removing dist and bundle.html.

remediation.issue: Binary component archive reduces audit transparency
remediation.suggestion: Replace the tar archive with checked-in source files, or publish a manifest and checksum for the archive.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts need clear execution boundaries
remediation.suggestion: Document expected working directories, file changes, and network installs before users run the scripts.

semantic_findings.title: Package Manager Installs Third-Party Code
semantic_findings.description: The setup and bundle scripts install or add third-party packages, including a global pnpm install when pnpm is missing. This can run npm lifecycle scripts and pulls current package versions at execution time.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly invoke npm and pnpm package installation commands. This is legitimate setup behavior, but it executes third-party package code from the network.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Build Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: The bundle script removes dist and bundle.html in the current project before building. The package and index checks reduce exposure, but the command can delete local build artifacts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rm -rf command is explicit and destructive, but it targets common generated outputs after project-root checks. This makes the issue real but bounded.

content.value_statement: Complex Claude artifacts often need state, routing, components, and a repeatable build setup. This skill scaffolds a React project and bundles it into one shareable HTML artifact.
actual_capabilities: Creates a Vite React TypeScript project with Tailwind CSS configuration.
Adds shadcn/ui components from the included component archive.
Configures TypeScript and Vite path aliases for local imports.
Installs Radix UI and related frontend dependencies.
Bundles a built React app into one self-contained HTML file.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later and a working package manager environment.
Downloads npm dependencies during setup and bundling.
Targets React artifacts, not simple static HTML snippets.
The bundle script must run from a project root with index.html.

best_practices: Review package installs before running the setup script in a trusted workspace.
Use this skill for multi-component artifacts that benefit from React state.
Bundle only after checking the app in a browser or preview tool.
anti_patterns: Using the setup script for a one-screen static HTML artifact.
Running the scripts in a directory that contains unrelated project files.
Assuming generated dependencies are safe without package review.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a React and TypeScript artifact project and bundles it into one HTML file.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts install npm packages during setup and bundling.

faq.question: Can it build simple HTML snippets?
faq.answer: It can, but it is better suited for complex React artifacts.

faq.question: Which UI library is included?
faq.answer: The setup includes shadcn/ui components and Radix UI dependencies.

faq.question: Where is the final artifact saved?
faq.answer: The bundle script creates a single HTML file in the project root.

faq.question: Should users review the scripts first?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts install dependencies, write configuration files, and remove build outputs.
